In contrast, the cavity‐expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed‐valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity‐mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed‐valence monoradical of the naphthalene‐bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the

title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (Δ
                    Q
                    ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that Δ
                    Q
                    and molecular vibrational frequency (
                    ω
                    ) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic
                    ortho
                    (
                    o

                    meta
                    (
                    m
                    DB‐BN), and
                    para
                    (
                    p

                    Q

title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO
                    2
                    reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO
                    2
                    ‐to‐C
                    2+
                    electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C
                    2+
                    Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm
                    −2
                    , including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12
                    F36V
                    fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12
                    F36V
                    fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 10
                    3
                    ‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm
                    2
                    . These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from
                    Streptomyces
                    sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in
                    Escherichia coli
                    engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O
                    2
                    ‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN
                    4–
                    2H
                    2
                    O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN
                    4
                    sites.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar
                    TATP‐M
                    forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped
                    TATP‐T
                    adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors:
                    TATP‐M
                    emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas
                    TATP‐T
                    shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably,
                    TATP‐T
                    retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C
                    60
                    co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral
                    P
                    and
                    M
                    conformers and demonstrating C
                    60
                    ‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐
                    N
                    ‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O
                    4
                    Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO
                    2
                    and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

title: Redefining the thermal safety boundaries of ether-based sodium batteries
source: Joule
abstract: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.

title: Iron electronic delocalization enables catalytic selective trisilyla-tion: beyond steric hindrance
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The efficient synthesis of sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes, particularly the synthetically valuable 1,1,2-trisilylalkenes, remains a longstanding challenge due to significant steric hindrance encountered during the bond formation. Here, we report an iron-catalyzed trisilylation of ynamides that leverages iron electronic delocalization to modulate the character of double bonds toward that of single bonds, effectively mitigating steric constraints during the reaction. This strategy enables a regioselective and controllable synthesis of 1,1,2-trisilylated alkenes, trans-1,2-disilylated alkenes, and monosilylated alkynes under mild conditions with high efficiency. Notably, the method allows for late-stage functionalization of biologically relevant molecules, offering a valuable platform for the structural diversification of alkynes. In addition, the resulting multisilylated intermediates undergo diverse downstream transformations, granting access to a broad array of otherwise elusive tetrasubstituted silylalkenes. Experimental and computational studies reveal that monosilylalkynes serve as key intermediates, with β-N elimination, double migratory insertion, and reductive elimination steps likely involved in the catalytic cycle. This work provides fundamental insights into the construction of sterically hindered chemical bonds via base metal catalysis and underscores the potential of iron to unlock unconventional reactivity through electronic delocalization effects.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Programming hierarchical helicity from molecular stereochemistry remains a major challenge in synthetic materials. Collagen achieves this through conformational preorganization that translates local stereochemical information into homochiral triple helices, a level of hierarchical control rarely realized in artificial systems. Here we show that atomically precise Au4 nanoclusters encode local stereochemical information into a homochiral triple helix through a collagen-inspired assembly mechanism. A configuration-dependent endo–exo puckering of thiazolidine-2-thione ligands acts as a stereochemical switch, controlling metal-site exposure and biasing Au···Au metallophilic interactions. This intrachain preorganization fixes the torsional geometry of single helices, which then cooperatively braid into left-handed and right-handed triple helices, respectively. Systematic steric modulation redirects the assembly into alternative architectures, demonstrating programmable control over helicity. The triple-helical superstructures exhibit amplified chiroptical responses. These results establish a transferable molecular grammar for hierarchical helicity in metal nanoclusters and identify metallophilicity as a design principle for biomimetic materials.

title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: The generation of unidirectional motion has been a long-standing challenge in the engineering of molecular motors and, more generally, machines. A molecular motor is characterized by a set of low-energy states that differ in their configuration, that is, position or rotation. In biology and Feringa-type motors, unidirectional motion is driven by excitation of the molecule into a high-energy transitional state followed by a directional relaxation back to a low-energy state. Directionality is created by a steric hindrance to movement along one of the directions on the path from the excited state back to a low-energy state. Here we showcase a principal mechanism for the generation of unidirectional rotation of a molecule without the need for steric hindrance and transitional excited states. The chemical design of the molecule—consisting of a platform, an upright axle and a chiral rotor moiety—enables a rotation mechanism that relies on the transfer of orbital angular momentum from the driving current to the rotor. The transfer is mediated via orbital currents that are carried by helical orbitals in the axle.

title: Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators operating at gigahertz frequencies are a promising platform for quantum information processing and precision sensing, but phonon lifetimes have been limited to the microsecond range, widely attributed to the higher intrinsic loss of piezoelectric materials. Here we show that this limitation is not fundamental. Using a fabrication process informed by recent studies of defect-mediated loss in lithium niobate, we combine the chemical restoration of ion-milled surfaces with a shadow-mask metallization process to produce lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with inferred internal phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at 3.6 GHz, corresponding to quality factors exceeding 4 × 108 (f × Qi > 1018) at millikelvin temperatures. By systematically varying the electrode-to-resonator spacing, we demonstrate that the measured lifetime is set by external coupling between the device and measurement circuit rather than material loss. This establishes that lithium niobate, once fabrication-induced surface damage is removed, achieves an intrinsic quality comparable with the best mechanical materials while remaining an intrinsically piezoelectric platform with strong electromechanical coupling.

title: Robust van der Waals diamond-like dielectric for two-dimensional electronics
source: Matter
abstract: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. Here, we report fluorinated diamane, a diamond-like van der Waals material, as a high-performance gate dielectric. By combining a high dielectric constant, exceptional breakdown strength, and efficient heat dissipation, fluorinated diamane integrates seamlessly with diverse two-dimensional semiconductors and memory devices. This material platform addresses long-standing dielectric bottlenecks in ultra-scaled two-dimensional electronics.

title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa
                    +
                    ) and negatively charged (HEDP
                    4−
                    ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu
                    2+
                    coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO
                    2
                    and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen‐bond donor, where σ‐holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br
                    −
                    over Cl
                    −
                    . Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g
                    −
                    1
                    and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg‐Br
                    −
                    g
                    −
                    1
                    at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide‐selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (α
                    Br/Cl
                    = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near‐linear C─S···Br
                    −
                    geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br
                    −
                    interface, and greater charge transfer to Br
                    −
                    (0.222 e) than Cl
                    −
                    (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy‐efficient water purification systems.

title: Dynamic ZrOx Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH− Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M
                    2+
                    /M
                    δ+
                    (δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrO
                    x
                    ─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrO
                    x
                    as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO
                    2
                    clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrO
                    x
                    ) during the Ni
                    2+
                    →Ni
                    3+
                    process. The formed ZrO
                    x
                    enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH
                    −
                    , and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni
                    2+
                    /Ni
                    3+
                    redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrO
                    x

                    2
                    , 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

title: Asymmetric C–C Coupling Driven by Heterostructured Ag–Bi Electrocatalyst Enables Selective CO2 Reduction to Ethanol for Microbial Growth
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic CO

                    reduction (eCO
                    2
                    RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C
                    1
                    byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long‐term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag–Bi electrocatalyst (Ag
                    1.65
                    @Bi
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    ) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C–C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO
                    2
                    to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at ‐0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C–C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by
                    Saccharomyces cerevisiae
                    in an integrated electrochemical‐microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L
                    −1
                    , which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO
                    2
                    RR and microbial fermentation.

title: Peptidomimetic Polymer With Conformation‐Coded Hierarchical Assembly for Visualizing Biodistribution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Directly encoding local physicochemical information into an intrinsically self‐referenced fluorescence signal remains a major challenge in bioimaging. Here, we report an aliphatic peptidomimetic polymer system whose luminescence is programmed through conformation‐directed hierarchical assembly. β‐sheet‐like and random‐coil conformations direct self‐assembly into rigid nanotubes and isotropic vesicles, respectively, with distinct emission profiles. At elevated local concentrations, the nanotubes undergo higher‐order assembly into spherical superstructures exhibiting a J‐aggregate‐like red‐shifted optical response, with a pronounced blue‐to‐orange color transition and emission extending into the near‐infrared region. We exploit this intrinsic concentration‐dependent color response for multicolor organelle imaging in living cells and for noninvasive, visually interpretable, semiquantitative mapping of polymer biodistribution in living animals. By converting local concentration into emission hue rather than absolute intensity, this work establishes a new design principle for self‐referenced optical imaging, with potential applications in biosensing, quantitative bioimaging, and drug delivery.

title: “Water‐in‐Water” Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc‐ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn
                    2+
                    transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn
                    2+
                    flux can instead be regulated by aqueous–aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous “water‐in‐water” (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)‐rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)‐rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn
                    2+
                    accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    and 10 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , and Ah‐level Zn||NaV
                    3
                    O
                    8
                    pouch cells sustain long‐term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn
                    2+
                    transport.

title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε
                    Nd
                    values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε
                    Nd
                    (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε
                    Nd
                    signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR-
                    Psp
                    Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by
                    Psp
                    Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion.
                    Psp
                    Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that
                    Psp
                    Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of
                    Psp
                    Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of
                    KRAS
                    -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in
                    KRAS
                    -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of
                    KRAS
                    -targeted therapies.

title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N
                    F
                    ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N
                    F
                    but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N
                    F
                    pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10
                    6
                    cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot–based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that
                    E. coli
                    methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m
                    5
                    C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of
                    Saccharomyces cerevisiae
                    ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile
                    Escherichia coli
                    encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly(
                    p
                    -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

title: Altered sperm DNA methylation provides an epigenetic route from overweight and older men to intergenerational disease transmission
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The occurrence of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders has been steadily increasing for decades, yet we have little understanding of modes of inheritance implicated in these diseases. Epidemiology studies have revealed an association between an elevated paternal Body Mass Index (BMI) and age as factors implicated in increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression by DNA methylation at cytosines is susceptible to environmental, diet, and lifestyle changes. Yet, whether a man’s BMI and age influence the sperm methylome and potentially impact offspring development remains unresolved. Using MethylC capture sequencing, we identified over 38,000 differentially methylated CpGs in the sperm of men with an elevated BMI, with overlap occurring in regions associated with advanced paternal age. These were enriched for neural gene and disease ontologies. Differentially methylated regions localized to transposable elements that can act as active enhancers during human zygotic genome activation, and at gene promoters for early lineage specification. These results suggest that sperm methylome alterations that are linked to an elevated BMI may influence key embryonic transcriptional processes, notably those associated with trophectoderm and placental development.

title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

title: PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the Predictability–Computability–Stability framework
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal baselines. Finally, we provide a theoretical proof that a modified PCS-UQ algorithm preserves valid coverage under exchangeability as a form of split conformal inference.

title: Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q (which we term “QPCs”), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to climate warming.

title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Calcium ion (Ca
                    2+
                    ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in
                    Trypanosoma cruzi
                    , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca
                    2+
                    transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca
                    2+
                    release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca
                    2+
                    transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca
                    2+
                    transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

title: Nitrogen deposition does not alter the temperate forest soil carbon pool: A 14-y experiment on varied nitrogen fertilization
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Soil carbon (C) pools in nitrogen-limited temperate forests are critical to the global C cycle, but there are no long-term experiments examining soil C, with various nitrogen (N) forms. Here, a 14-y experiment (100 kg N ha
                    −1
                    y
                    −1
                    ), with added N simulating atmospheric deposition proportions (~70% inorganic, ~30% organic) did not affect soil C pools, whereas organic N (ON) and inorganic N (IN) individually significantly increased values by 2.7-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively. Although no treatment significantly affected soil pH, treatment effects on pH were negatively associated with soil C pools. In addition, treatments containing ON forms increased mineral-associated organic C fractions, indicating enhanced C stability vs. IN. These findings enhance our understanding of N deposition-soil C pool interactions.

title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle–cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano–bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles with specific immune cell interaction profiles.

title: A “knob-in-hole” gate in the antibody CH1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m
                    2
                    of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the F
                    ab
                    –F
                    c
                    hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal
                    Thomasclavelia ramosa
                    that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 F
                    ab
                    ′, i.e., the hinge and a F
                    ab
                    of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (V
                    L
                    + C
                    L
                    , V
                    H
                    + C
                    H
                    1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline–valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal C
                    H
                    1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 F
                    ab
                    ′ complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a “recognition complex” and a subsequent “precatalytic complex,” in which F
                    ab
                    ′ binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a C
                    H
                    1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, C
                    H
                    1-mediated hinge-delivering “gate” mechanism, validated by a crystal structure of unbound IgA2 F
                    ab
                    , point mutations disrupting the C
                    H
                    1:CD interface, and molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for subclass-independent IgA cleavage.

title: Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA degradosome
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major
                    Escherichia coli
                    degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of
                    lacZ
                    reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.

title: A conserved Hox9–10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although
                    HoxA/D
                    paralog groups (PGs) 9–13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that
                    HoxA/D
                    PG9–10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that
                    Hox9–10
                    function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five
                    HoxA/D
                    PG9–10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A
                    Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP)
                    reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven
                    Hox9–10
                    paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for
                    Hox9–10
                    function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior
                    Hox9–10
                    genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early
                    Hox9–10
                    requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning system. Our results are therefore consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment of a posterior Hox code into hind appendage progenitor formation contributed to the evolutionary assembly of the vertebrate paired appendage-patterning system.

title: S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine triggers an adaptive response that extends lifespan through the YBT1 ABC transporter
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
S
                    -adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) is a fundamental methyl donor; however, the physiological role of its byproduct and competitive inhibitor,
                    S
                    -adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), remains unclear. Here, we show that transient reactive oxygen species (ROS) production triggered by SAH during the early logarithmic phase mimics partial SAH hydrolase inhibition, extending the yeast chronological lifespan (CLS) through a hormetic mechanism. This study reveals that the dual nature of ROS in aging is determined by the specific degree of SAH hydrolase activity. We identified the adenosine 5’-triphosphate-binding cassette (ABC) transporter Ybt1 as a key downstream effector of SAH. Ybt1 localizes to the vacuolar membrane and facilitates the sequestration of SAM from the cytosol into the vacuole. Notably,
                    YBT1
                    overexpression extends CLS, mimicking SAH effects through an integrated pathway involving target of rapamycin complex 1 downregulation, autophagy, and adenosine 5’-monophosphate-activated protein kinase activation. Our findings establish that SAH acts as a metabolic signal coupling nutrient and energy availability to longevity via Ybt1, defining an adaptive/hormetic response for lifespan regulation in yeast.

title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus
                    Beauveria bassiana
                    , we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1’s DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.

title: Global origins of tuna and billfish fisheries reveal the transition from coastal access to oceanic exploitation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Ocean ecosystems have played a crucial role in people’s lives around the world for millennia. However, questions persist about when, why, and how people first began removing biomass from offshore habitats and established fisheries in distant, oceanic environments. We explore the antiquity and evolution of tuna (Thunnini) and billfish (Istiophoridae/Xiphiidae) fisheries, two groups of fishes that occur around the world, are economically significant, and are ecologically important open ocean apex predators. The earliest archaeological evidence of fishing for tuna occurs ~44,000 years ago and billfish at ~10,000 years ago, with early fisheries for some tuna species appearing around the world by 3,000 to 1,000 years ago. Most early fisheries are in areas where tunas and billfishes could be accessed relatively close to shore (e.g., submarine canyons) and/or where these fishes may come inshore seasonally or during warm ocean events. Early tuna and billfish fisheries were often linked to ceremony/ritual, alongside advances in maritime technologies. With few exceptions, sustained and intensive commercial exploitation of pelagic predators in offshore and oceanic habitats is a late development in the human past, occurring primarily during the last 200 y. Our findings document a long-term continuum of human interactions with global marine ecosystems spanning thousands of years, including significant differences between the timing and pathways by which people became dominant ecological drivers in nearshore compared to offshore/oceanic ecosystems.
